sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: purpose of the safety section, the big picture, the cost of collisions, side scanning, rural hazards, when to look behind, space management, courtesy merges, side clearance, passing one vehicle, dangerous situations, other drivers' errors and road rage habits
Confusable pairs and continuation facts; each block ties to one manual page, and any hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec14-R01 | anchor: A01
Section C of the manual is devoted to safety tips for safe driving and for sharing the road with others. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec14-R02 | anchor: A02
Get the big picture by keeping a proper following distance so you can judge the real hazards around your vehicle, and do not tailgate. [A02]
Why it matters: group five habits; confusable big picture versus aim high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec14-R03 | anchor: A02
Communicate in traffic using your horn, lights, and signals to make eye contact with motorists and pedestrians, and be reasonably sure of people's intentions [A02].
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec14-R04 | anchor: A02
New drivers need practice and experience to turn the manual's written guidance into habits, so the manual advises reviewing it often. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec14-R05 | anchor: A03
Even a collision with no injuries brings inconvenience and repair bills and can lead to court, fines and higher insurance rates, so a clean record protects you financially. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec14-R06 | anchor: A03
Scan from side to side for directional signs and for cars or people that could be in the road by the time you get there. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec14-R07 | anchor: A03
In rural areas, watch for hidden intersections and driveways, curves, hills and changing road surfaces such as pavement turning to gravel or a narrowing road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec14-R08 | anchor: A03
Look at the traffic to your rear before a lane change, before backing, before braking hard and on long steep downgrades. [A03]
Why it matters: group mirrors; confusable when to look behind versus how often.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec14-R09 | anchor: A03
When you track how fast and where the traffic is on every side of your car, you can decide quickly and safely in most situations. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec14-R10 | anchor: A03
Communicating in traffic means making your next move clear to drivers and pedestrians in time for them to avoid a collision [A03] [A04].
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec14-R11 | anchor: A04
Controlling the space around you may mean slowing down or speeding up, but only within lawful limits. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec14-R12 | anchor: A04
You can help keep a following driver at a safe distance by holding a steady speed and signaling early before you slow down or turn. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec14-R13 | anchor: A04
On multi-lane roads, be courteous and move to the left lane when other vehicles are trying to merge into traffic. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec14-R14 | anchor: A04
Leave extra space between your vehicle and parked cars, pedestrians and bicyclists at the roadside, especially children. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec14-R15 | anchor: A04
Cutting across several lanes at once can tie up traffic, cause you to crash, or cause a crash between other drivers trying to avoid you. [A04]
Why it matters: group merging; confusable one lane at a time versus cutting across.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec14-R16 | anchor: A04
As a general rule, pass only one vehicle at a time, and do not pass unless there is room to return to the driving lane. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec14-R17 | anchor: A04
When finishing a pass, do not count on the other driver to make room for you; you need enough space behind you to return safely. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec14-R18 | anchor: A04
Allow extra space when vision is blocked for you or another driver, for example by bushes at an intersection, glaring sun or pedestrians with umbrellas. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec14-R19 | anchor: A04
Allow extra space around drivers or pedestrians who are distracted by phones, roadside attractions, sightseeing or tending to children. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec14-R20 | anchor: A05
Allow extra space around confused drivers or pedestrians, such as those weaving between lanes, hunting for street names or reading maps. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec14-R21 | anchor: A05
Slow down and leave room for drivers merging suddenly around road hazards, from ending lanes, or onto and off expressways. [A05]
Why it matters: group driver errors; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec14-R22 | anchor: A05
Slow down and leave room for drivers who may be forced into your lane by another merging vehicle, road construction or emergency vehicles on the roadside. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec14-R23 | anchor: A05
The manual cites the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration as saying about 66 percent of yearly traffic deaths are caused by aggressive driving such as passing on the right, running red lights and tailgating. [A05]
Why it matters: dated statistic; dynamic.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec14-R24 | anchor: A05
Law enforcement agencies and insurance companies are getting much tougher on aggressive drivers. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec14-R25 | anchor: A05
To avoid road rage, obey the law, drive defensively, drive relaxed and within the speed limit, do not tailgate, and pass only when you need to. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec14-R26 | anchor: A05
If you are harassed on the road, try to get the offender's license plate number and report the incident to the authorities. [A05]
Why it matters: group road rage; confusable being followed versus being harassed.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec14-R27 | anchor: A05
A driver who tends to get angry behind the wheel must change that attitude and behavior, or becomes a crash waiting to happen. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0109]
